Methods and means of organizing the introduction of network delays as part of the emulation system of MEC platforms LWMECPS were analyzed. Test applications mec-test-app and mec-test-client are developed for testing and evaluation of the introduced network delays. Developed mec-orch-app to provide test application management and metrics collection. Experiments have been conducted to estimate the insertion latency and manage the test applications using mec-orch-app. Special attention was paid to the organization of all parts of the system as a future laboratory bench for testing decision systems using reinforcement learning machine learning algorithms.

articleTitle: Studying tne Frequence Dynamics of the Power System and Determining tne Constant Frequency Based on WAMS
abstract: The relevance of the work lies in the need to maintain the frequency of the power system in continuous mode. High sudden load in the system causes a volume imbalance, which in turn leads to a deviation from the nominal frequency. A frequency deviation of 0.2 Hz no longer meets the power quality requirements. Reducing the frequency is dangerous because it reduces the transmission speed of electric motors and the principles driving them, which causes a decrease in their productivity, a violation of the technological conditions of consumers and leads to defective variable products. Wide area measurement system (WAMS) allow real-time monitoring of the electrical parameters of the power system, including frequencies. Objective. Consider changing the frequency when an imbalance occurs, the method for determining a constant frequency. Perform analysis and calculation of constant frequency based on WAMS. Compose model functions and calculate the frequency constant, compare with the data from the initial calculation. METHODS. Was used the Fourier transform method, according to which we moved from the frequency function to its spectrum, which makes it possible to simply determine the frequency constant. RESULTS. The article describes the relevance of the topic and examines the dynamics of frequency behavior. The constant frequency was calculated using the WAMS data and compared with the constant frequency of the simulated functions. CONCLUSION. Using this method allows, in the presence of WAMS data, to determine the constant frequency, which allows us to understand how the system will behave if a power imbalance occurs.

articleTitle: Stages of Developing an Adaptive Model of a High-Efficiency Gas-Piston Mini-CHP Complex with Energy Storage Units Operating Under Electric and Thermal Load Schedules
abstract: Distributed generation (DG) is widely implemented in the structure of distribution networks (DN), leads to the connection of innovative energy units (EU), increasing the efficiency of both business processes with reduced energy tariffs and DG facilities. Operation of EU of mini-CHPs in the generation mode leads to redistribution of electric power (EP) flows in the external network and causes the need for optimization of the structure and modes, checking the switching capacity of the equipment. EP accumulators in power output schemes (POS) increase the efficiency of use of the entire complex of equipment (CE) of mini-CHPs, as well as equalize load schedules in the DN. The purpose of the study is to develop the sequential stages of formation of a highly efficient CE with gas-driven units (GDU) and energy storage units (ESU) of a mini-CHP for a specific consumer, for the subsequent long-term operation of the facility, taking into account its daily and seasonal consumption. To solve this problem, it is necessary: to analyze consumption by means of online monitoring and to develop a methodical approach to the selection of the whole CE; to create an adequate and adaptive model of operation of the POS of mini-CHP and adjacent DN; to develop an expert online system of identification and support of operating modes of CE by modules of operational and predictive analytics. The material presents the structural and functional scheme of the developed expert system of control modes and diagnostics of mini CHP CE (ESCMD) and adjacent 10/0.4 kV DN.

Author Keywords: expert system of control modes and diagnostics

articleTitle: Evidences Extraction and Analysis Challenges
abstract: With each passing day, the incidence of cybercrimes targeted at various organizations is on the rise. Concurrently, the approaches to committing such crimes are evolving, notably through the development of new malicious software and the employment of novel tactics and techniques for malicious activities. This evolution necessitates the modernization of the investigation process as well as enhancing the efficiency of professionals working in this field. This article examines and organizes the challenges encountered during the investigation of cybercrimes, particularly in the extraction and analysis of evidence. Based on an analysis of these challenges, unified algorithms for the stages of evidence extraction and analysis are developed, which can be applied in both the scientific and technical domains, specifically in the investigation of computer crimes. It is anticipated that the proposed algorithms will increase the efficiency of the investigation stages under consideration and will serve as a starting point for the development of specific and general methodologies for cybercrime investigation.

articleTitle: Studying How the Configuration of a Genetic Algorithm Affects the Solution of a Problem
abstract: This paper discusses a genetic algorithm - an approach to solve complex optimization problems in a reasonable amount of time. It describes the principle of operation of the algorithm. The algorithm's efficiency is demonstrated by approximating the popular knapsack problem. The influence of each of the algorithm's parameters on the obtained solution is studied by freezing the other parameters and simulating an NP-complete problem with a known solution. It is concluded that the algorithm needs to be properly configured for the best results - its parameters individually don't have a decisive impact on the final solution, but in conjunction perform very well. It is also concluded that the genetic algorithm proves to be extremely effective in finding a close enough solution to the optimal one for NP-complete problems.

articleTitle: On the Issue of Comparing Magnetic Fields and the Output Signal in Magnetostrictive Converters of Linear and Angular Displacements Using Solenoids in the Form of a Spiral and a Cylindrical Shape
abstract: The article is devoted to the issue of comparing magnetic fields and output signals formed by spiral-shaped and cylindrical solenoids in the acoustic paths of magnetostrictive linear and angular displacement transducers. Studies related to the refinement and derivation of appropriate formulas and expressions have been carried out, computational experiments and experimental checks have been carried out. It was found that the amplitude value of the playback signal from a linear amplifier with a spiral coil is less than the playback signal of a cylindrical solenoid and in computational experiments amounted to 20-25%. The results of experimental studies have shown that the signal from the spiral coil is 20% less than the signal from the cylindrical solenoid. This decrease in the signal can be compensated by significantly reducing the inter-turn distance. The reliability of the theoretical results and computational experiments obtained in the article is confirmed by experimental studies. Since magnetostrictive sensors containing solenoids are used in many fields and fields, including robotics, the article has a practical focus and presents prospects for further research.

articleTitle: The Analysis of Images of Mathematical and Chemical Formulas from Patent Documents
abstract: Currently, patent documents contain graphic images of device drawings, graphs, chemical and mathematical formulas, and the formulas often need to be recognized and brought to a unified standard. This work analyzes graphic images extracted from the descriptions of FIPS Rospatent patents. Thematic filtering of mathematical and chemical formulas contained in patent documents and their recognition is provided. The theoretical value lies in the developed patent parsing algorithms in the Yandex.Patents system; recognition of chemical and mathematical formulas among graphic patent images; converting graphic images of chemical formulas into SMILES format; converting graphic images of mathematical formulas into LaTeX format. The practical significance of the work lies in the developed software module for analyzing graphic images from patent documents. The scope of the developed module is the study of patents and the reduction of graphic images to a unified standard for solving patent examine problems.

articleTitle: Digital Equivalent Load Monitor for Rolling Mill Motors
abstract: The reversing stands of plate rolling mills are made with individual (direct) roll electric drives to ensure the independent adjustment of their speeds. Launching new rolling profiles and optimizing rolling mill programs require improved calculation methods for the equivalent motor currents and torques. The available methods are based on the processing of smoothed load diagrams per one rolling cycle that are deemed the same for the main electric drive motors of the upper and lower rolls (UMD and LMD). This does not account for the differences in actual loads that may be 2–3 times different under the steady rolling modes. These differences lead to overloads, increased wear of electromechanical systems, and reduced motor efficiency. To avoid these drawbacks, the authors justified a calculation algorithm for the equivalent loads of motors using the parameters measured directly during rolling. The algorithm was tested on a 5000 plate rolling mill adjusted using the previously developed virtual control system commissioning procedure using digital twins. The authors present the results of the processing of UMD and LMD motor current and torque arrays obtained during the rolling of a five-piece batch. Some conclusions were made about the reliability of the results obtained and the efficiency of the practical application of the developed load monitor. The authors demonstrated that the equivalent LMD torque and current have smaller changes than the same figures for the UMD. This can facilitate the optimization of rolling programs and the improvement of the load division regulator algorithm.

articleTitle: Automated Penetration Testing Based on Adversarial Inverse Reinforcement Learning
abstract: This article is a study of modern trends in information security from the point of view of vulnerability analysis; the application of the Adversarial machine learning method is considered Inverse Reinforcement Learning (AIRL) in penetration testing. Integration of semantic rewards into the AIRL framework is proposed for deeper modeling of attacker strategies. The article analyzes the problems of penetration testing and proposes tools for collecting expert data, such as Deep Exploit, and discusses the prospects for using AIRL to train agents in dynamic network infrastructures. A model of an automated system for collecting expert data and penetration testing based on Adversarial Inverse Reinforcement Learning is proposed. The method used provides more effective simulation of vulnerabilities and increases the system's adaptability to modern information attacks and a changing environment. The use of AIRL with semantic rewards can significantly improve information security processes and provide new tools for analyzing the effectiveness of countering complex evolving cyber-attacks.

articleTitle: Application of Machine Learning Methods to Determine the Movement of a Car Using a MEMS Accelerometer Signal
abstract: Currently, automobile security systems use remotely controlled electronic relays that break the vehicle's electrical circuits, the operating algorithms of which require autonomous determination of the vehicle's motion/rest states. Due to price restrictions on the implementation of relays, the role of motion sensors is played by MEMS accelerometers. When installed in the engine compartment, the accelerometer measures the acceleration of movement against the background of vibrations from a running engine and from uneven road surfaces, and the spectral composition of the signal depends on the make of a particular car. It is proposed to individually configure the parameters of the machine learning algorithm for each car, which classifies the states of motion/rest. When setting up the algorithm, statistical processing of acceleration in the motion/rest sections is first carried out, and a set of informative parameters are selected that are used in the formation of the training sample. The results of the classification algorithm based on the support vector machine method are presented at various sampling rates of the acceleration signal and sliding window sizes for extracting informative parameters.

articleTitle: Development of Project Management Module for Reflex Cloud IDE
abstract: Paper describes a project management module for the Reflex process-oriented language cloud IDE. Currently, a prototype IDE called RIDE has been developed for the Reflex language, based on Eclipse Theia. This implementation approach allows the user to launch the IDE in a browser and immediately begin developing embedded control software. However, Theia is aimed at single-user applications and this drawback limits complexity of the programs. Therefore, Reflex IDE requires a development environment, which provides sufficient features for group development. The paper analyzes existing cloud IDEs and multi-user collaboration in projects, formulates architectural requirements for the project management module, and describes the implementation of the cloud IDE RIDE using the Reflex language.

articleTitle: Modeling Attacks on Machine Learning Components of Intrusion Detection Systems
abstract: Intrusion detection systems (IDS) perform a critical security function and can detect both known and unknown and more complex attacks. However, intrusion detection systems based on machine learning mechanisms (primarily deep learning) are susceptible to so-called adversarial attacks. This study examines the impact of attacks on the machine learning components of intrusion detection systems used in complex heterogeneous infrastructures by simulating such attacks. Various machine learning models are presented to detect anomalies in most cases used in intrusion detection systems. For the first time, a simulation of an adversarial attack on the machine learning components of IDSs was carried out. The dependence of the influence of the FGSM attack on the efficiency metrics: Precision, Recall, f1 was built.

articleTitle: Optimizing DC Link Capacitors in Three-Level Voltage Inverter Based on Space-Vector PWM with Seven-Stage Switching Sequence
abstract: The voltage imbalance of the neutral point (NP) of the DC link is one of the key factors restricting the use of three-level autonomous voltage inverters with a fixed neutral point in electric drive systems. The NP voltage imbalance leads to reduced inverter output voltage (current) quality and increased voltage surges in DC link capacitors, which inevitably affects the reliability of the power elements of the inverter circuit. Reducing the NP voltage imbalance requires increasing the capacitance of capacitors, which, in turn, results in the greater weight and dimensions of the three-level inverters, as well as increased costs. To solve this problem, the authors of this paper suggest a new control algorithm for the three-level inverted based on space-vector PWM with a seven-stage switching sequence (SS) that facilitates a threefold reduction of DC capacitor capacitance compared to the conventional algorithm due to controlling the duty factor of distributed base vectors in each of the PWM period based on the displacement angle and load data. This article presents a calculation procedure for the operating time of the base vectors in the seven-stage SS, taking into account the impact of small and medium base vectors and load parameters. The efficiency of the proposed algorithm is confirmed with computer modeling in MatLab & Simulink. The proposed algorithm provides a significant improvement in the technical parameters of three-level voltage inverters, especially in high-power electric drive systems.

Author Keywords: three-level neutral point clamped voltage source inverter

articleTitle: Existing Approaches & A Proposal to Content Analysis of Pilots' Speech Activities
abstract: Content analysis of pilot speech is a key tool for improving flight safety as it allows to identify potential problems in communication between pilots, dispatchers and crew. The development of efficient algorithms for analyzing pilot speech contributes to improving communication skills, preventing incidents and improving overall airline safety. The research focuses on the possibility of applying machine learning techniques and deep neural networks to analyze speech data, which opens new perspectives for information processing and interpretation. The results of the study emphasize the interdisciplinary nature of the topic and suggest new methodological approaches, including the use of fuzzy set theory and fuzzy logic systems to handle uncertainty in speech data, which in turn helps to improve communication performance in complex and stressful flight conditions. The finalization of the work includes the evaluation of the developed methods and approaches in terms of their applicability and impact on improving flight safety, incorporating model training results and addressing testing errors.

articleTitle: Digital Technologies for Assessing and Predicting the Impact of the Spatiotemporal Distribution of Greenhouse Gases on the Photosynthetic Activity of Crops
abstract: In this article a set of models for the formation of a new intelligent technology in the field of digital crop production is proposed by the researchers. It makes possible to determine the current and forecast values of the concentrations of greenhouse gases in ground layer of the atmosphere, as well as conduct a spatial-structural analysis of the existing and possible distribution of greenhouse gases in the study area on the basis of a series of virtual experiments, without the expense of material, natural, time and human resources traditional for natural experiments. A synthesized apparatus of artificial neural networks (considering various paradigms, identifying the best topology) and GIS tools were used for developing these models. To assess the predictive capabilities of the models, full-scale experiments were conducted in agricultural areas of Belgorod region. An analysis of the results of intelligent modeling in determining the optimal parameters of crop production was carried out. Software tools were developed.

articleTitle: Radio Navigation Algorithms for Tasks of Industrial Internet of Things
abstract: Increasing the bandwidth of modern cellular communication devices opens up new opportunities for automation and control of industrial processes. The minimization of wireless data transmission devices and data processing conducted with the help of cloud technologies and plant digitalization algorithms allows increasing the efficiency, safety and environmental friendliness of production devices. The integration of network technologies into data collection systems and cloud management of the actuator system is one of the steps towards the creation of Industry 4.0 systems where management and decision-making processes are conducted with the help of artificial intelligence algorithms. Determining the location of systems, devices and their nodes during the technological process implementation is an important task that becomes especially relevant with the introduction of robotic unmanned systems into technological processes. This paper discusses the possibilities of using navigation algorithms for the tasks of the industrial Internet of Things related to indoor navigation. The main areas of use of navigation tools are analyzed, as well as methods for integrating radar and radio navigation algorithms into the systems of Internet of Things and industrial Internet of Things. During the work, a robotic plafthorm with a naviagtion system, controlled via a cloud service, was developed and tested. At the same time, the methods of primary signal processing are considered to reduce the impact of fluctuations and interference in the system to the minimum. The experimental data obtained on a full-scale mock-up showed the effectiveness of the applied algorhithms.

articleTitle: Optimal Filtering and Extrapolation in Problems of Quick Security Assessment of Critical Information and Telecommunication Resources
abstract: The paper comprises the development of approaches to the construction of methods for quickly assessing the security of critical information and telecommunication resources. In the work, we use analytical processing of large heterogeneous data on the current and predicted security parameters. The purpose of the study is to develop a mathematical and methodological apparatus focused on methods of optimal filtering and extrapolation applied to security indicators for such resources. During these processes, the indicators vary both linearly and nonlinearly. The optimal filtering and extrapolation are conducted in terms of minimum mean square error. The core peculiarities of this approach are analyzed. The proposed approach allows the assessment of algorithms to learn and adjust the weighting coefficients of filtering and extrapolation to the statistical characteristics of the security indicators. Besides, the approach makes it possible to unify the assessment algorithms, thereby creating the prerequisites for unifying the algorithms for protection and resource management.

articleTitle: Location Monitoring of Overhead Power Lines Using a Lightning Protection Cable
abstract: The authors propose an intelligent location sensing system which automatically detects problems in the power supply network and takes measures to prevent accidents. The decision-making algorithm is based on pulse sensing of overhead power lines. The location equipment is connected to 35 - 750 kV air lines via connection filter and a high-voltage communication capacitor, which transmit technological information from relay protection and emergency automation equipment to the high-frequency path of the line. For overhead lines that do not have such equipment, location pulses can be applied via a lightning protection cable (ground wire) provided on 35 - 750 kV lines. Simulation of this process in PSCAD system shows that the energy of microsecond-long sounding pulses is sufficient for effective and reliable detection of damage to the line wires.

articleTitle: Dual Layer Cogni - Insight Deep-Mood Encoder: A Two- Tiered Approach for Depression Detection
abstract: Depression (MDD) affects approximately 5% of adults globally, contributing to productivity loss and public health concerns. With 280 million people impacted, the risk of suicide and self-harm underscores its severity. Current treatments are inadequate, and the complex, heterogeneous nature of depression necessitates automated solutions for timely assessment and varied treatments. This study explores the transformative role of Artificial Intelligence in detecting depressive symptoms, leveraging NLP, and multimodal data analysis. The research introduces the “Dual Layer Cogni-Insight Deep-Mood Encoder (DLCDME)” model, incorporating two-tiered feature encodings. Four pre-trained language models (BERT, MentalBERT, MentalRoBERTa, PsychBERT, and ClinicalBERT) are experimented and fused with linguistic features for comprehensive representation. A transformer encoder, multi-head attention, and LSTM fine-tuning enhances contextual text feature embeddings, demonstrating the efficacy of ClinicalBERT with transformer encoders for cost-effective large corpus handling. Contributions include a novel feature extraction approach, a thorough model analysis, and the superior performance of DLCDME over contemporary works, holding promise for clinical diagnosis. Our findings reveal that a) the application of ClinicalBERT over DLCDME significantly enhances the performance of depression detection, and b) employing dual feature encodings on text data with transformer attention for predicting depression yields an improved MAE of 3.40 and RMSE of 4.38. The model achieved a test accuracy of 95%, with F1 scores for precision, and recall recorded at 0.95, 0.96, 0.95 respectively.

articleTitle: A Method for Introducing Big Data into State Organizations
abstract: Big Data (BD) has already reached a plateau of productivity in a variety of business areas. Meanwhile, the input of BD to socio-economic development promoted by public administration is constrained by factors. The goal of the study is to find a method to apply BD to fulfil public objectives for Industry 4.0 development. The empirical base of the study is the business practices of BD usage in Russia, India, and Singapore. The study identified the barriers of BD diffusion in Russian public administration and state organizations. The regulatory inertia, specific requirements to data prevents the BD usage in solving of public issues. Considering the administrative essence of the barriers, a result of the research is the proposal of an administrative mechanism to support the BD leverage in public administration in Industry 4.0 development. The method of promotion BD potential for Industry 4.0 development consists in public and business partnership for BD processing. The method allows state organizations to employ best business practice to use BD for societal development.

articleTitle: Combined Information and Measurement System for Electricity Metering for Autonomous Hybrid VEI Stations
abstract: A combined information and measurement system for electricity metering for autonomous hybrid stations on renewable energy sources is presented; it consists of three main elements: primary measuring instruments - the first level; data transmission medium - second level; software for processing., storing and displaying data - the third level. Works in RS-232, RS-422 and RS-485 interfaces. Adapted to the lC:Enterprise 8 accounting environment using the lC-Energy Resources Accounting GUVS subsystem. Includes reference books: “Device Indicators”, “Scada Templates”., “ER Indicators”., documents: “Registration of installation of devices””., “Distribution of instrument readings by day””., “Registration of ER consumption”., automated workstations: “Consumer” desktop., “Metering devices”., “Download readings for the period”. Creates reports: “Primary readings of devices by consumers””., “Report of ER by consumers””., allows you to exchange data with 1 C-Accounting.

articleTitle: Hardware Cybersecurity on the FPGA Platform During Network Interaction of Distributed Industrial Equipment
abstract: This article discusses methods for reducing cyber threats in the network interaction of industrial equipment under DCS control. It is assumed that the control and network circuits of the equipment use solutions based on the FPGA platform. Methods of protecting network messaging are proposed by replacing separate, specially allocated network segments with uncontrolled access with a hardware-protected network segment (PNS). The PNS consists of two units with FPGA Cyclone 10 LP 10CL025YU256C8G from INTEL. In addition, each unit has an RS-485 Transceiver for connection to the RS-485 network segment and two DS-link LVDS-based Transceivers. An encryption algorithm in PNS for each bit of the transmitted byte of RS-485 data is proposed, in contrast to the widely used block encryption algorithms. DS encoding was used when transmitting data inside the PNS. The presented research focuses on the development and analysis of an effective implementation of a real-time data encryption algorithm. An example of the formation of code sequences during data encryption is considered.

articleTitle: Big Data Security Evaluation by Bidirectional Analysis of Access Control Policy
abstract: Big Data, the advanced technology that harnesses the value of huge volumes of varied data through real-time processing, is presented today in almost all areas of the smart industry. Big Data collection, processing, and storing use heterogeneous instruments and various types of data transforming operations. Big Data sustainability and security are tightly linked to smart industry security. Different data fragments migrating through a smart system contain semantically related information, and thus it is hard to trace data misuse along the data route. Such specifics are not concerned when evaluating cybersecurity and resiliency if applying conventional security evaluation techniques based on static, ontological, neural networking, risk-oriented or other types of analysis. This work proposes a novel technique for Big Data security evaluation that utilizes a data processing graph and a bidirectional analysis of data access. It performs the compliance of real access abilities with the given access control policy. A security evaluation framework prototype has been developed to automate our method and demonstrate its opportunities.

articleTitle: Alternative Resource-Saving Current Protections for Electric Motors
abstract: In the article the author presents the principle of operation of alternative resource-saving maximum current and longitudinal differential protections, the purpose of which is to protect high-voltage electric motors from external and internal short circuits. The presented protections are performed without the use of widely used in the electric power industry measuring current transformers (CT) with metal cores, which have significant weight and dimensional parameters and high cost. The proposed protections are made using magnetically controlled elements such as reed switches and inductance coils. Protections with their application can be used as an alternative to traditional motor protections and at the same time are not inferior to them in terms of speed. The developed protections represent an innovative approach in realization of relay protection of various electrical installations. Resource-saving of these protections is in the use of inductive coils and reed switches, which are, both in terms of cost and weight and dimensional parameters, an order of magnitude cheaper and smaller in size and weight than the above-mentioned current transformers. Protections are recommended for use in high-voltage electric motors, presented in the form of maximum current protection (MCP) and differential protection against multiphase short circuits and internal faults. The proposed protections are performed in the form of devices, with their installation inside the cell of complete switchgear (complete switchgear), voltage 6–10 kV and electric motor. The use of the presented protections increases the reliability relay protection, as protected electric motors, and the cell of the complete switchgear.

articleTitle: Development of a Method for Generating Extremely High Reference Motion Speeds of Mechatronic Objects Moving Alone or in a Group
abstract: The paper presents the results of developing a method for generating reference control signals that describe the desired law of movement of various mechatronic objects (unmanned aerial vehicles, mobile land and underwater robots, etc.) along smooth trajectories specified by parametric splines. In order to maintain high dynamic accuracy of control of these mechatronic objects, including when solving group control problems, it is proposed to adjust their reference movement speed, taking into account the specified restrictions on the developed accelerations. Taking into account these restrictions is necessary to reduce the reference speed in sections of the trajectory with increased curvature. To implement the proposed approach, a method was developed and a system was synthesized, the performance of which was confirmed by the results of numerical simulation. The presented system is designed to operate in conditions where the reference trajectory of a mechatronic object is unknown in advance and is formed (or adjusted) directly during the mission without the possibility of preliminary calculations. Also, this system does not require complex calculations and can be implemented on the basis of low-power on-board computers.

articleTitle: Parallel Processing of SQL Queries Using MPI.NET
abstract: The article focuses on a solution for parallel processing of SQL queries in relational databases. It explores the use of MPI.NET and EF Core to address the challenges posed by increasing data volumes in various industries. The article emphasizes the effectiveness of MPI.NET in parallel data processing and its integration with parallel algorithms. It includes tests with real data and scenarios, confirming the efficiency and applicability of the developed approach. The solution demonstrates significant scalability and performance, making it highly suitable for modern data processing demands. The authors detail the implementation and advantages of using MPI.NET and EF Core in handling large-scale data, ensuring high performance and efficiency in contemporary information technology environments.

articleTitle: On Linear Envelopes Calculation for Traffic Flows in Industrial Control Systems
abstract: Nowadays, industrial control systems are falling squarely under the Industry 4.0 dominant trends and technological challengers. In this, the problems associated with data, their processing and analysis happen to be particularly serious. Among all data issues, data flows, most commonly called traffic flows, cause a deep concern since they are crucial for the correct real-time system functioning, and the knowledge of their characteristics is decisive for the assessment of critical time performance measures such as delays in alarm presentation and control action transmission. In order to explore industrial control system traffic flows and to calculate time performance measures, a theory of deterministic queuing systems Network calculus is worth to be utilized. The article is devoted to industrial control system traffic flows and the Network calculus application to them. In particular, the approaches to estimating envelopes for traffic flows are considered. The concept of envelopes on finite intervals is introduced, and their linear model is expounded. The advantages of linear envelopes on finite intervals over classical minimal envelope are revealed, and the algorithm for their online calculation is analyzed. The basic features of typical traffic flows encountered in upper-level control systems of nuclear power plants are outlined, and the results of the investigation of their deterministic envelopes as well as statistical indicators are presented. Conclusions are drawn about the legitimacy and practical acceptability of using linear envelopes on finite intervals in the applications of industrial control systems.

articleTitle: L/STIM: A Framework for Detecting Multi-Stage Cyber Attacks
abstract: The number of cyber-attacks is growing every year, and the attacks themselves are becoming more complex. Multi-step attacks are a separate category. Their peculiarity is that they are performed in several stages, are often aimed at many nodes and affect many devices. Thanks to deep learning models, it became possible to automatically deliver the context of events from chains of records about the state of the system. Neural networks show high efficiency in the process of establishing relationships when analyzing data with a large number of features. The paper presents the L/STIM framework, which is designed to identify multi-step attacks using a combination of big data processing methods and machine learning. Thanks to short-term and long-term analysis, L/STIM is able to detect multi-step attacks with a long execution period with an accuracy of up to 98% on a binary classifier and up to 82% on a multi-class classifier.

articleTitle: Recognizing Railway Infrastructure Using CNN and Stereoscopic Vision
abstract: In the era of Industry 4.0, achieving Grade of Automation 4 (GoA 4) within the railway sphere is pivotal for the development of autonomous networks. This necessitates intelligent systems capable of real-time perception, precise object identification, and accurate determination of distances. This paper investigates railway object detection using Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), specifically the YOLOv8 architecture, extending prior research by integrating CNN with stereoscopic vision for distance determination to the detected objects. Implementing GoA 4 enables autonomous systems to interpret and react within railway environments. Our evaluation of YOLOv8 demonstrates consistent and robust object detection, achieving an mAP of 0.8 at IoU 0.5 and maintaining 0.54 across IoU 0.5-0.95. Utilizing stereoscopic vision, the determination of distances to detected objects within a 250-meter range exhibits an error margin of less than 10%, ensuring high precision in distance estimation. The integration of YOLOv8 with stereoscopic vision for accurate distance estimation, executed within 80 milliseconds, demonstrates remarkable computational efficiency, which is crucial for real-time applications. This efficient process, facilitated by the Nvidia RTX A5000 graphics accelerator, ensures both precision and high speed in dynamic railway settings. Our assessment emphasizes the adaptability and reliability of YOLOv8 in detecting railway infrastructure objects across diverse conditions, signifying its potential for real-world deployment.

articleTitle: GREMC: Genetic Reverse-Engineering of Machine Code to Search Vulnerabilities in Software for Industry 4.0. Predicting the Size of the Decompiling Source Code
abstract: The article is devoted to the problem of security of cyber-physical systems as part of production according to the Industry 4.0 concept. For this purpose, the author's approach of “Genetic Reverse Engineering of Machine Code” (GREMC) is proposed. The essence of this approach lies in the use of artificial intelligence in the field of genetic algorithms to restore the source code of software executed in the form of machine code on cyber-physical devices for Industry 4.0. The resulting code can then be analysed for vulnerabilities by an expert. One issue that arises during genetic reverse engineering is predicting the size of the source code based on its machine representation (i.e., in an object or executable file). The article is devoted to solving this problem for functions in the C programming language. To do this, a method for obtaining a relationship between the sizes of the source and machine code of individual functions is described, which consists of steps such as loading a dataset with C-functions, isolating the function code in it, preprocessing them, compiling them into machine code, calculating the required sizes, building dependencies between each source code size and the corresponding machine code sizes, generating the final table and determining the dependency formula. An experiment is carried out using a software prototype that implements the method; ExeBench with 83 thousand C-functions is taken as a dataset. Justifications are given regarding the appearance of abnormal machine code sizes and their impact on the dependence formula.

articleTitle: Development of an UAV System Architecture Using Machine Vision Algorithms with a Single-Board Computer or FPGA
abstract: This paper presents the development of an unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) control system architecture based on a single-board computer or FPGA with a neural network. The main focus is on integrating neural networks into UAV flight controllers to enhance control efficiency and reliability. The paper describes the methods and approaches to implementing such a system, as well as analyzes potential benefits and issues that may arise with its use. The outcomes of this research may benefit scientists and engineers in the fields of avionics and artificial intelligence and contribute to the advancement of UAV technologies.

articleTitle: Methods and Software Tools for Generating Waypoint-Driven Motion Profiles for Highly Automated Vehicles Using Q-Learning
abstract: The burgeoning market for Highly Automated Vehicles (HAV) is witnessing rapid expansion across various sectors. A pivotal challenge impeding the reduction of costs and development time for HAV control systems is the intricate process of developing and fine-tuning a motion profile-a comprehensive array of attributes and parameters delineating the operational and control strategies of HAVs under assorted road conditions. The primary objective of this research is to devise methodologies and instruments that expedite the development of the HAV path-following subsystem. This acceleration is achieved through the employment of Q-learning algorithm for the creation of the HAV movement profile within the confines of task-specific constraints. Optimization of the motion profile is done by increasing the weight of the required performance indicators in the reward function during the learning process. The effectiveness of the described approach is confirmed by the construction of two motion profiles, taking into account the terrain slope, designed to minimize fuel consumption or maximize average speed. Testing of the resulting motion profiles in the simulator showed their expected differences, allowing one to achieve target performance indicators. The approach described in the work for the generation of an optimized motion profile using Q-learning methods claims scientific novelty. The practical value of the described approach is the reduction of the HAV development process time due to the absence of the need to build a model that accurately describes the behavior of the car in the context of solving the optimization problem

articleTitle: Technologies of Human Digital Twins as a Basis for Decision Support for Strategic Planning of Territorial Development
abstract: The purpose of the study is to analyze and classify data to create a reliable human digital twin - a subject of economic relations, as well as develop models for collecting, transmitting, integrating, processing of this data to build an architecture of a human digital twin to intelligently support the process of strategic planning of territorial development. The differences between the human digital twin and the machine digital twin are highlighted. Data sources are analyzed and data classification is proposed for creating a human digital twin. The authors proposed a model of an integrated multi-level architecture of a human digital twin. The process of supporting decision-making on strategic planning of territorial development based on the technologies of a digital human twin, an agent-oriented approach, the use of ontologies that ensure the reliability of forecasts for the development of the macro system was modeled.

articleTitle: Obstacle Avoidance Method with Local Semantic Map Generation for Self-Driving Cars
abstract: When implementing a control system for a ground-based highly automated vehicle (HAV) used in agriculture, a significant factor is the low cost of the equipment used, so cameras using without lidars for navigation, avoiding obstacles, and ensuring movement safety seems promising. Ensuring the safety of movement of HAV consists of developing methods and tools that allow to avoid static and dynamic obstacles and make an emergency stop if it is impossible to avoid. The main problem when using cameras is the lack of information about the distance to objects. The article describes methods and software tools that allow transforming an image into a top view (birds-eye-view) projection, and use information about free space for movement along with information about obstacles in order to improve the quality of obstacle avoidance algorithms compared to classical methods that use frontal projection. Object detection implemented with YOLOv8 neural network, free space for movement detects with semantic segmentation tool based on MobileNetV3 network architecture, also software tools for combining several data sources to build a local perception map are developed. Linear and angular speed of the HAV based on calculating the optimal direction of movement for avoiding obstacles. Testing of the developed methods and software implemented in the Webots simulation environment. Software developed with ROS2.

articleTitle: Medical Recommendation System Based on Collaborative Filtering Algorithms
abstract: The article deals with the issues of designing a medical recommendation system based on the collaborative filtering algorithm. The problem under consideration is a large number of medical errors, which are one of the most common causes of patient deaths. In Russia alone, more than 70 thousand people suffer severe complications every year for this reason. The aim of the research is to analyze the possibility of designing and implementing software that reduces the probability of occurrence of medical errors and allows to realize the automation of prescribing by a doctor of the optimal treatment for a particular patient. The article analyzes the subject area and problem situation, identifies the causes of a large number of medical errors in public medical institutions in Russia. The problem statement is considered, mathematical support of the recommendation system based on the algorithm of collaborative filtering is proposed. The analysis of methods for solving the problem is given. The implementation of the recommendation system in the Python programming language is considered, the results of research in the form of a computational experiment are analyzed and interpreted. According to the results of the research, it is concluded that the proposed implementation of the medical recommendation system based on the collaborative filtering algorithm can be used in the further design of a full-fledged system and then used in medical institutions as a part of the system.

articleTitle: Optimization of Power Transformer Defect Recognition Algorithm with Dga Based on Probabilistic Neural Network
abstract: The trouble-free operation of power oil-filled transformer equipment is impossible without an effective diagnostic system. It is generally recognized that the chromatographic analysis of gases (DGA) dissolved in oil is the most informative method for diagnosing the condition of oil-filled transformers. Nowadays, it is increasingly being implemented as continuous online monitoring. In this case, new methods of processing and displaying the flow of diagnostic parameters and analyzing the ratios of key gases, with the interpretation of their palette and accuracy in making a “diagnosis” to prevent emergency conditions will be in demand. A method of forming an adaptive diagnostic model for TO based on online monitoring data with a cluster database for IESD is proposed. Organization of offline and online monitoring subsystems, scaling of object models and server process based on PostgreSQL are described. The advantages of probabilistic neural network (PNN) for non-normal distribution of diagnostic results are highlighted. The Moth Flame algorithm for optimizing weights within the model is described.

articleTitle: Applying of Pre-Trained SotA CNN Models at a Local Enterprise for Human Identification: Comparative Analysis of Accuracy
abstract: This study examines the possibility of using modern neural network models that perform human recognition from photos at a local enterprise with up to 30 people. The participating models are FaceNet, FaceNet512, SFace, ArcFace, DeepFace, VGG-Face and Dlib from the DeepFace Framework. A feature of the study is the variation in the number of source photos in the database (1, 4, 8, 16 pieces per person), on the basis of which we can draw a conclusion about the accuracy and ease of use of a particular model in a real task. Accuracy is assessed by evaluating the F1 score at precision> 0.75. At the same time, threshold is assessed for each case and the performance of the networks under consideration. The work provides tables and graphs of the dependences of F1 score on the number of people, the number of photos per person, the neural network model used and metrics. As a result, a conclusion is made about the possibility of using FaceNet and FaceNet512 (30 people, 16 photos per person, cosine, F1 > 0.96, 90–100 ms per photo) and SFace (30 people, 16 photos per person, cosine, F1 > 0.8, 17 ms per photo). Moreover, both FaceNet models can be used for a database of 30 people, even if there is one photo per person (cosine, F1 > 0.94).

articleTitle: Features of Creating a Virtual Laboratory for Developing and Applying Correlation Rules in Modern SIEM-Systems when Training Security Operation Center Analysts (by the Example of Microsoft Windows)
abstract: This paper proves the necessity of using a specialized virtual laboratory for effective training of future Security Operations Center (SOC) analysts. The lack of adequate information resources and integrated technical means complicates the training process and hinders the development of professional skills of trainees. The authors analyze the peculiarities of creating a virtual laboratory at the university and the advantages of its implementation in the educational process for the development and successful application of correlation rules in modern SIEM systems. As a result of the research, the necessary conditions for the functioning of the virtual laboratory were identified, which allows students not only to study modern technologies of anomalous activity detection, but also to develop and apply in practice correlation rules for SIEM-systems on the basis of conducting and analyzing various attacks on the Microsoft Windows operating system.

articleTitle: Technical Statistics Processing for Performance Management in Cellular Networks
abstract: The cellular operator is based on a complex telecommunications infrastructure consisting of a large number of network devices. Performance monitoring of such networks is a very resource-intensive and difficult task. The performance monitoring process collects and processes large amounts of technical statistics and logs, from which radio network engineers can form an idea of the current network performance status. Based on the information obtained, cellular operators can quickly detect, locate and repair network problems, as well as carry out regular activities on the network to improve overall network performance. However, traditional methods of data processing and storage are not applicable due to the special qualities of the collected data, determined by its large volume and high intensity of its receipt. Thus, it is necessary to use big data technologies. This article offers a general description of a platform, designed to meet the challenges of telecommunications service providers, in particular the monitoring of network performance.

articleTitle: Top-20 Weakest from Cybersecurity Elements of the Industry Production and Technology Platform 4.0 Information Systems
abstract: This work is dedicated to the issue of constructing secure information systems, which form the foundation of any industrial and technological platform within the Fourth Industrial Revolution (Industry 4.0). It addresses and solves the task of identifying weak elements in such systems at the design stage by leveraging accumulated data regarding vulnerabilities from the National Vulnerability Database (NVD). It reviews existing literature on the analysis of NVD content, highlighting a lack of suitable solutions. To tackle this issue, the paper proposes a method based on linguistic and statistical processing of vulnerability descriptions. This method includes several steps: downloading NVD vulnerabilities for each code, consolidating these vulnerabilities into a unified structure and preprocessing them, extracting descriptions and measures of their impact on information security threats (breaches of confidentiality, integrity, and availability), breaking down the descriptions into constituent elements of information systems and their post-processing, collecting statistics on word occurrence in descriptions and their impact on breaches, generating a top list of the most vulnerable elements, and saving the final results. A programmatic prototype implementation of the method (in Python) is described. An experiment is conducted to compile a Top-20 list of the most vulnerable elements of information systems, both in general and in terms of their impact on all three information security threats. The paper analyzes the four resulting lists, discusses the limitations of the conducted research and results, provides justifications, and indicates ways to overcome these limitations.

articleTitle: Digital Twins of Document Archives
abstract: The article proposes to use the concept of digital twins to address the problem of the archival storage of various types of documents. Even though the provided literature review demonstrates the active use of digital twins primarily in industrial manufacturing and partially in other spheres of economy and society, the use of digital twins in archival storage is still not considered. However, the criticality of the preservation of information and valuable documents in the era of digital transformation increases significantly, as information and digital data have become key production factors in Industry 4.0. The article proves the relevance of using digital twins of document archives. The article identifies the challenges of archival storage, demonstrates the need to improve the efficiency of archival storage by using digital twins. The author formally formulates the task of documents archival storage management with the help of digital twins. Mathematical models for the control of conditions of archival storage, as well as technologies for the control and restoration of documents, are proposed. The necessity of using 3D/4D printing and artificial intelligence technologies is addressed. The assessment of the efficiency of archival preservation using digital twins is performed. The practical application of the suggested approach is reviewed, and the lines of future research are defined.

articleTitle: Properties of 5G Video Conference Traffic and Short-Term Forecasting of Input Data Rate
abstract: In this article, we outlined the goals and prospects for short- and long-term data traffic forecasting in 5G networks. The study provides an overview of current traffic forecasting methods. A large number of works indicate a variety of approaches to the analysis and forecasting of mobile traffic. These approaches include both traditional statistical methods and deep learning methods, which is an important factor for the development of network technologies and optimization of radio access networks. Using mobile traffic data from Google Meet, MS Teams and Zoom video conferencing systems as an example, we studied the features of this type of traffic and came to the conclusion that the distribution of time intervals between the arrival of packets corresponds to an a-stable distribution. Having studied some machine learning methods designed for time series forecasting, we performed a comparative analysis of the effectiveness of these methods for short-term forecasting of data traffic intensity.
